records.real_world_identity_notes: Lola T95/00 of the 1995 IndyCar season, a chassis raced with Ford/Cosworth XB and Mercedes-Benz IC108 engines among others, fitted with a six-speed manual gearbox.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.
records.identity_basis: A registered source establishes the chassis and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
records.specification_basis: The source gives a six-speed gearbox for this chassis, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick with automatic cut and no automatic blip.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established the six gears through a sequential stick, the standing-start clutch, the clutchless running shifts, automatic cut, and no automatic blip.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts, no automatic blip, and a clutch needed to pull away, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.

This class runs three configurations rather than two: base, high downforce and Speedway. Speedway is an oval package, which is why the suffix differs from the downforce pairs used elsewhere in the dataset.
This car was observed in all three of the class's configurations, so it anchors the identity format for the others.

additional_telemetry_names.basis: Base configuration of the same car, observed exactly in live telemetry. AMS2 selects the configuration from the circuit, so a driver reaches this identity without choosing it. Controls are inherited from the driven high-downforce configuration and were not separately tested.

Speedway configuration of the same car, observed exactly in live telemetry. AMS2 selects the configuration from the circuit, so a driver reaches this identity without choosing it. Controls are inherited from the driven high-downforce configuration and were not separately tested.

additional_telemetry_names.basis: Base configuration of the same car, recorded in SimHub's stored inventory from an earlier observation and matching the derivation from this car's observed high-downforce name. AMS2 selects the configuration from the circuit, so a driver reaches this identity without choosing it. Controls are inherited from the driven high-downforce configuration and were not separately tested.

Speedway configuration of the same car. This exact string was not observed: it is derived from the car's observed high-downforce identity by replacing the suffix. Lola T95/00 Ford-Cosworth was seen in all three of this class's configurations and the same derivation reproduces its observed names exactly. AMS2 selects the configuration from the circuit, so a driver reaches this identity without choosing it. Controls are inherited from the driven high-downforce configuration and were not separately tested. If the derivation is wrong the identity simply never matches, which is what a driver sees today.
